items.title: Enforce the configured senior and junior funding ratios
items.description: ## Summary create_tranches stores senior_pct, but invest_tranche never checks it while increasing filled amounts. A schedule described as 70% senior and 30% junior can accept all recorded investment into the senior class because no target principal or class capacities exist. Add explicit quotas for a defined invoice target so the configured ratio corresponds to an enforceable risk allocation. This is a funding-policy enhancement, separate from settlement distribution after funding completes. Code reference: [contracts/invoice-tranche/src/lib.rs:88](https://github.com/StellarState/SS-contracts/blob/2e480a6e77a31ac2d03f26086ae1ab19b513c85b/contracts/invoice-tranche/src/lib.rs#L88). ## Scope - Bind creation to an invoice target and derive class capacities. - Reject or partially fill investments exceeding remaining class quotas. - Define deterministic rounding for indivisible targets. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] A 70/30 schedule with target 100 accepts at most 70 senior and 30 junior units. - [ ] Filling one class does not block the other available class. - [ ] Repeated calls apply cumulative class capacity. - [ ] Small targets preserve the funding total despite rounding. - [ ] Rejected investments leave positions and filled totals unchanged. - [ ] Tests cover full funding, oversubscription, mixed investors, and minimum-unit rounding. Related work: #663 introduced ratios; this enhancement makes the descriptive configuration enforceable during funding. ## ETA 24 hours

items.title: An agent whose MCP tools failed to load is silently cut off; the agents page should show it
items.description: **What happened:** in one agent session, an MCP server's tools failed to load. Its listing errored with "listing their tools failed". The session ran on with none of that server's tools and no visible sign. It only came to light when the agent was asked to read its inbox on that server. The same session's Den tools were also one version behind the running Den (0.4.76 against 0.4.77). **Effect:** in a group of agents, that member was silently unreachable on the server's channel. The lead couldn't tell, and the member couldn't reply there. **Expected:** - The agents page shows, per agent, which MCP servers failed to load their tools, with the error, and flags an agent whose Den tools are older than the running Den. - Opening that agent offers the restart that fixes it, since a restart keeps the conversation. - A lead (or the person) can see that a member can't be reached before handing out work. **Steps:** start an agent session while one MCP server's tool listing fails. Keep using the session and note that nothing shows it. **Versions:** Den 0.4.77 running, the session's tools at 0.4.76; macOS.

Its session list, conversation, clip, card, image and send payloads go, with the attachment store, the session overlays, the chat and voice script injection, the standalone send probe and the vendored screenshot script. hubmux stops the overlay injection in the same change and passes on no session handler. The live stream keeps its run, board and chart subjects and offers no session subject. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The GET routes under `/api/sessions` reach no session code. - [ ] The POST routes for send, card answer, attach, voice and screenshot reach no session code. - [ ] An unknown GET serves the page and an unknown POST answers 400, as before. - [ ] The hub starts with the `session_send` and `sessions` build facts removed. - [ ] hubmux injects no session overlay and passes on no session handler. - [ ] The live stream sends run, board and chart updates. - [ ] The live stream offers no `sessions` and no `conversation` subject and watches no transcript. - [ ] One test lists every removed method and path pair and proves that none reaches session code. - [ ] That test runs on the hub and through hubmux with a loaded profile prefix, from loopback and from an admitted tailnet identity. - [ ] The Slack settings route and the operator spend in the Spend panel answer as before. ## Blocked by - #2490 (the phone page calls these routes; it must stop first)

items.title: Backend in Rust: groundwork and a route-by-route move off Python
items.description: The backend (`src/wednesday`, about 13k lines of Python) could later move to Rust, replacing the PyInstaller-bundled server the Tauri shell starts as its sidecar (#92). The aim is a smaller installer (no bundled pandas / scikit-learn / pyarrow), a faster start and one language for the shell and the server. Not now: this issue tracks the groundwork that makes the move cheap and safe, then the move itself, route by route. ## Why it can be done in steps The dashboard (`web/`) and the shell only talk to the server over HTTP on `127.0.0.1`, through 57 `/api` routes. A Rust server that answers the same routes with the same JSON can replace the Python one without changing either. The database (SQLite or PostgreSQL through `storage.py`) stays as it is, so the trader's settings, drawings, journals and history carry over. ## Groundwork (in Python, now) - [x] **1. Lock the API contract.** A test that lists every route and snapshots the shape of each GET response and each request body, so a change to the API shows up as a failing test with a diff. The Rust server is later checked against the same file. - [x] **2. Reference data for the detectors.** Candles in, expected levels and setups out (order blocks, BSL / SSL, inducement, ranking, sessions, quarters), as JSON in `tests/`. Any port must give the same output on the same candles. - [x] **3. Keep detector logic pure.** New detector code works on plain lists and dataclasses, not pandas, so it translates line by line. - [x] **4. Remove the Lab.** Decided: the Lab (labelling, training, scikit-learn models, the ML layer on the chart) goes, replaced by a call to an external API. That drops `scikit-learn` and `pyarrow` from the installer and leaves no pickle models to port. - [x] **5. Plugin interface.** Decide how the paid plugin loads without Python entry points (dynamic library or WASM), and keep the core's hooks small. ## The move (in Rust, later) - [x] **6. Rust server in front.** Serves the routes it has ported and passes the rest to the Python sidecar, so the app works at every step. - [x] **7. Port the core first:** M1 to 4H–5M resampling (closed candles only), detectors, setups ranking, sessions and quarters. Checked against the reference data (2). - [x] **8. Port storage and settings** (`sqlx`, SQLite and PostgreSQL, same schema), drawings, workspaces and templates. - [ ] **9. Port the rest**, in this order (least tied to the engine first): - [x] ~~9a. The login and API tokens~~: dropped, the login was removed (

items.description: ## Parent - Parent packaging slice: https://github.com/intersoftdatalabs-in/percussioncms/issues/1978 - Grandparent: https://github.com/intersoftdatalabs-in/percussioncms/issues/962 - Packaging PR (landed packaging dual-ship proof): https://github.com/intersoftdatalabs-in/percussioncms/pull/1988 ## Why residual #1978 packaging dual-ship verification is agent-safe and done in PR #1988. **Live root Linux soak** is agent-unsafe / ops-owned and was explicitly deferred. ## Dual-ship policy (do not reverse) **Keep init.d** until this soak passes and ops review completes. Do **not** implement #1976 deprecation/removal of init.d in this issue. ## Soak checklist (CMS + at least one DTS role) ### CMS (`jetty/service/install-jetty-service.sh`, unit `PercussionCMS`) - [ ] Install on a real Linux host from a build that includes PR #1988 packaging - [ ] Confirm layout ships `jetty/service/` (`install-jetty-service.sh`, `percussion-cms.service.in`, `README-systemd.md`) - [ ] systemd path: `install` → `systemctl enable/start/status/stop` → `journalctl -u PercussionCMS` - [ ] Long start / upgrade simulation: no false fail solely on timeout before 30 minutes (`TimeoutStartSec=1800`) - [ ] `--initd` only install on a systemd host (no dual boot registration conflict) - [ ] Uninstall clean (no leftover unit or SysV links / `/etc/default` / init.d) - [ ] Migration: init.d-only → uninstall → systemd reinstall ### DTS (Production and/or Staging) - [ ] Confirm install places role script + `dts-tomcat.service.in` under `Deployment/Server/` - [ ] Same systemctl start/status/stop/journal checklist for `PercussionProductionDTS` or `PercussionStagingDTS` - [ ] `--initd` only + uninstall clean + init.d→systemd migration ## Acceptance - [ ] Checklist signed off (or defects filed) on this issue and linked from #1978 / #962 - [ ] No silent single-path-only packaging regression (packaging already gated in #1988) ## Out of scope - Removing init.d (#1976) - Agent-automated live root systemctl on customer hosts

items.title: Separate lifetime fee attribution from available treasury balances
items.description: ## Summary get_treasury_balance returns TotalBalance with SourceBalance values described as a per-source breakdown. receive_fee increases both, but allocate decreases only TotalBalance. After receiving 100 and allocating 40, the total is 60 while the source value remains 100. That is useful as lifetime attribution but is not a breakdown of available funds. Make semantics explicit and expose reconciled availability separately from cumulative receipts so downstream reporting cannot confuse inflow history with spendable balances. Code reference: [contracts/treasury-management/src/lib.rs:132](https://github.com/StellarState/SS-contracts/blob/2e480a6e77a31ac2d03f26086ae1ab19b513c85b/contracts/treasury-management/src/lib.rs#L132). ## Scope - Name lifetime receipts and available balances unambiguously. - Expose received, allocated, and available amounts as reconciled concepts. - Define deterministic source debits if available balances are attributed per source. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Receiving 100 and allocating 40 reports availability of 60 and allocations of 40. - [ ] Lifetime receipts remain 100 when exposed separately. - [ ] Any available-source breakdown sums exactly to the available total. - [ ] Multi-source allocations follow the documented attribution policy. - [ ] Rejected allocations change neither balances nor history. - [ ] Tests reconcile repeated inflows, partial allocation, complete allocation, and overspending. Related work: #644 introduced treasury accounting; this enhancement clarifies source inflows versus availability after allocation. ## ETA 12 hours

items.title: Implement real per-server rootless Podman MCP runtime lifecycle
items.description: ## Goal Replace the current fail-closed placeholder with a real, deployment-owned per-server rootless Podman runtime. Do not enable shared-Hub execution as a fallback. ## Verified current gaps (PR #162 head 7034df47ec807213ea1767ce0a6f2a77156d4b82) - `mcp-hub-runtime.mjs` always calls `connectMcpStdioServer()`; no runner-profile selection is wired. - `mcp-runtime-supervisor.mjs` rejects every transport except `stdio` and has no isolated runner lifecycle contract. - `assertMcpRootlessRunnerAvailable()` always throws `MCP_ROOTLESS_RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` once reached. - `createMcpPodmanTransport()` starts an immutable image ENTRYPOINT but has no validated MCP application contract for registry command/args/config or scoped credentials. - Current Podman transport tests use mocked spawn/probe and do not prove a real MCP server runs inside a rootless container. ## Required implementation 1. Define a strict deployment-owned server-ID -> immutable runner-profile mapping. Never accept image, command, args, cwd, mounts, or runtime settings from registry/user input. 2. Define an authenticated, framed Hub runner MCP stdio protocol with bounded message sizes, deadlines, and explicit initialize/listTools/callTool behavior. 3. Design scoped credential delivery that does not place secrets in Podman CLI args, container environment, logs, image layers, shared mounts, or host-visible plaintext files. Fail closed if the chosen secret channel cannot meet this requirement. 4. Extend the supervisor with explicit runner create/connect/inspect/terminate lifecycle, cancellation, capacity accounting, execution draining, and verified cleanup on every startup/stop/failure path. 5. Add Linux integration tests using actual rootless Podman and a disposable test MCP server image. Cover initialize, listTools, callTool, stop, timeout, container crash, cleanup, cross-server isolation, and secret non-disclosure. 6. Keep feature disabled unless runtime capability and integration prerequisites are verified. No stdio/shared-Hub fallback. 7. Run full CI and an independent security review after implementation. ## Acceptance evidence - CI logs from a Linux runner with real rootless Podman (not mocked spawn/probe). - Test evidence that container IDs/processes are isolated per registered server and removed after stop/failure. - Redaction/leak tests for all control arguments, environment, logs, and diagnostics. - Exact deployment profile and secret-channel documentation. ## Related - PR #162: https://gith

items.title: Add bounded pagination to accreditation renewal reminder scans
items.description: ## Summary check_accreditation_reminders loads the complete WalletList and loops through every wallet and reminder log in one invocation. Without page limits or continuation, cost grows with registrations and eventually requires the transaction budget to accommodate the entire population. Add a bounded scanning interface allowing operators to complete daily sweeps in several calls while preserving interval suppression. This changes execution scale without changing reminder thresholds or the renewal-cycle semantics addressed separately. Code reference: [contracts/accreditation-renewal/src/lib.rs:93](https://github.com/StellarState/SS-contracts/blob/2e480a6e77a31ac2d03f26086ae1ab19b513c85b/contracts/accreditation-renewal/src/lib.rs#L93). ## Scope - Provide capped page size and continuation over registered wallets. - Define sweep membership when registrations occur during scanning. - Keep writes and events idempotent across repeated pages and retries. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Each invocation examines no more than the configured wallet limit. - [ ] Continuation reaches every wallet in the defined sweep membership. - [ ] Retrying a page does not duplicate emitted interval events. - [ ] Mid-sweep registration follows documented inclusion behavior. - [ ] Operators are authenticated and malformed cursors fail explicitly. - [ ] Tests cover multiple pages, retries, end-of-list, membership changes, and bounded resource use. Related work: #661 introduced scanning; this enhancement adds continuation for growing wallet populations. ## ETA 24 hours

items.title: Ask HN: Should Uber Ratings Decay over Time?
items.description: I’ve been thinking about how platforms like Uber calculate reputation scores, and I believe there’s a fundamental flaw in how historical ratings are treated. Uber calculates passenger ratings using the last 500 rated trips, regardless of when those trips occurred. In my case, I have 455 ratings, 426 of which are five stars (93.6%). My overall rating is 4.86. What bothers me isn’t the score itself, but the underlying methodology. A negative rating from five years ago can carry exactly the same weight as one received yesterday. And if you’re an infrequent user who hasn’t accumulated 500 ratings, that negative feedback could influence your reputation for years. This raises an interesting question: Should reputation systems measure your historical average, or should they attempt to represent who you are today? One possible solution is exponential time decay: Weight = 2^(-t/H) Where t is the age of the rating and H is a half-life, perhaps 12 months. Under that approach, a rating from one year ago would carry 50% of its original weight, and one from two years ago just 25%. Of course, this introduces other challenges. How do you prevent someone with a history of poor behaviour from simply waiting for their reputation to recover? How do you maintain statistical confidence for infrequent users? Would Bayesian smoothing or a minimum effective sample size help? There’s also a broader philosophical question around the right to be forgotten. Should digital reputation systems indefinitely preserve the consequences of historical assessments, particularly when those assessments are subjective and potentially no longer representative? I’m curious how others would approach this. * Is a rolling window of 500 ratings statistically defensible without considering time? * Would exponential decay produce a fairer and more predictive reputation score? * Should platforms expose both a lifetime rating and a recent-behaviour rating? * Are there better approaches already being used in other reputation systems? I’d be particularly interested in perspectives from people who’ve worked on marketplace ranking, trust and safety, or reputation algorithms. It seems like a relatively simple mathematical change, but one with potentially significant implications for fairness across digital platforms.

items.title: Ask HN: Where do you see Software in 5 years?
items.description: I wanted to hear some good opinions on all things AI and how they transform the Software industry. I'm anxious about the future and lack the foresight to form any opinion on what to do next. For context, I'm a L4 SWE that has more or less say 5-10 yrs of exp. I've enjoyed my work throughout my career, AI makes me ship more, much more than I could do 3 years ago. I feel I use it well and it translates into really good software. That said, what do you think happens in years to come with the Software industry in general? Do you think we'll go through a massive erosion of jobs? What's your perspective on that? I'm asking because I honestly don't know what to do: I can try to always keep up to date with newest technologies, best practices, but I'm only me; if the demand for SWEs and jobs falls to the floor, I'm not sure I'll always get a place at the table (i.e. land a job) and I'm wondering whether I should try to do something else in some other industry. It feels weird to be in a good position in life and still constantly worry about it getting worse.
